title: "Kloge Søren" (Søren Christensen), his Cyprianus, a book of charms in his own cipher, c. 1858 (catalogue 2525, KB Copenhagen, DFS 1997/020): simple substitution validated on a held-out portion, read in part

documents.shelfmark: Copenhagen, Det Kgl. Bibliotek, Dansk Folkemindesamling, DFS 1997/020 (Kloge Sørens samling); KB Digitale samlinger object392246, IIIF DFS_1997_020_4_000a to _107 (each image in its own folder on kb-images.kb.dk; the URLs are in the viewer page HTML)
documents.route: Søren Christensen, "Kloge Søren" (1843-1925), cunning man of Funen, writer and owner; a working book, not a letter

plaintext.source: Ferdinand Ohrt's copy and decipherment, recorded in the 1977 inventory of the collection (G. Henningsen; quoted by H. Nørgaard 2008, fynhistorie.dk/node/16123): 'Afskrevet og tydet af Ohrt. = kop 79.4'. Not consulted; not used. The writer's own table of the cipher alphabet is on image 091 left.

transcription.source: KB Digitale samlinger / IIIF images, 4,115 px per opening (first session) and full size 4,115 x 6,804 px per page (second session); images not reproduced
transcription.notes: Claude Opus 5.5 agents, 11 Nov 2026. Training pages 003 R - 007 L and the held-out images 030-031 transcribed sign by sign (notation in transcription.txt; the held-out files frozen and hashed before decoding). The 136 full-resolution pages were read straight into letters with the validated key, unresolved words kept in sign shapes (decryption.txt, Part 3). Two blind sheets of sign shapes answered by Brice Dudout: K1 (image 031) and K3 (nine targeted signs of the rest of the book); K2 (a random draw) abandoned before it was shown. Length counted in cipher words by the reading rule (8,055); signs counted only for the training portion (1,591) and the held-out portion (790). Integration check, 12 Nov 2026: images 030-031 and 003-008 re-read at full size (8,230 px per opening) against the writer's table; corrected signs of the held-out words in transcription.txt Part 2b (the frozen files are unchanged). The frozen held-out transcription disagrees with the reading in roughly one sign in ten (verifier: 85% of characters agree, 93% with a and e merged). Word count after the corrections: 425 (first session, contributor's count) + 176 (held-out, was 179) + 7,451 = 8,052.

system.summary: A private sign alphabet of the writer: one sign per letter, word spaces kept. Chevrons (a, e dotted), bars under 1-3 dots (u, n, m), strokes with dots above, beside or below (s, k, h, b, p), hooks (d, g, r, i/j), a cross (t, also f), an arch (v), dots (o, ø); ligatures aa, tt, nn, mm. Headings partly in clear Danish.
system.notes: Homophony or confusion t/f (cross), o/ø, i/j. The writer's table on image 091 left gives the alphabet a to ø in order. A circular seal in the same signs (018 R, 019 R, 104) is not read. The key is in the volume: the table on 091 left has 26 signs in three rows (10 + 11 + 5), a-k, l-v, x y z æ ø (seen at full size at the integration check); by the contributor's record it was found after the key had been recovered and measured.

prior_solution.where: Ferdinand Ohrt's copy and decipherment ('Afskrevet og tydet af Ohrt. = kop 79.4'), recorded in G. Henningsen's 1977 inventory of the collection, quoted by H. conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (every decipherment goes to Daniel; a partial reading may be published if explained; protocol hashed before one single measurement; blind re-reading by sign shapes), and answered the blind sheets K1 and K3. Claude Opus 5.5 agents transcribed, found and validated the key, read and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, key, annealing, protocol, measurement, reading by 16 sub-agents, write-up)

solution.what: Training pages 003 R - 007 L transcribed sign by sign at 4,115 px (1,591 signs); word spaces found visible.

Probable words guessed from the genre and the layout (no plaintext at hand): '3 gange' after the clear numeral, the trinitarian close 'i Navnet Gud Fader, Gud Søn og Gud den Hellige Aand. Amen', the cipher ordinals 'Andet / Tredie Begreb'; then a blind annealing (simple substitution, Danish quadrigrams with space, only the space fixed) found the plaintext by itself (6 of 10 restarts, contributor's figure; the annealing script is not in the PR).

One pre-registered measurement on the held-out images 030-031 (790 signs, transcribed and hashed before decoding): COV 0.4025 vs best of 200 permuted keys 0.1089 and of 200 sign shuffles 0.1038; C1-C3 and S met (C1 narrowly). Contributor's run. The verifier's re-run with another lexicon gives 0.404 against 0.157 (permuted keys) and 0.117 (shuffles): the +0.25 margin over the permuted keys is then 0.247, a hair short.
Held-out portion read by sense: 85.8% at once; image 031 right lines 16-26 re-read at full resolution: 96.1% (after the measurement, not blind).

Blind re-reading by sign shapes (sheet K1: 28 questions, 2 controls passed), rule hashed before the sheet: held-out portion 94.97% by the rule as written, 94.41% with Brice Dudout's remarks (result B, retained, declared deviation). Frames too tight: 3 of 5 losses from segmentation.

Second session: the rest of the book (007 R, 008 R - 079 R, 098) read at full resolution by 16 sub-agents, one fiche per page: 6,438/673/76/264 of 7,451 words = 95.4%. Image 091 left found to be the writer's table of the alphabet, confirming the key. Whole book 95.2% of 8,055 words, before any blind re-reading of this session.

Targeted blind re-reading by sign shapes of the second session (sheet K3: 9 signs chosen for the words whose class depends on the answer + 2 controls passed; rule hashed before the sheet, SHA-256 0400d3cf...; answers 4fbf5ec1...). Three probable words became certain, two unresolved; one ('før', 033 L) gives 'fer' by the rule with Brice Dudout's remark (result B, retained, declared deviation) but 'før' by sense, kept doubtful. Whole book 95.16% -> 95.13% (B; A 95.12%), indicative only; held-out portion untouched. The random sheet K2 was abandoned before it was shown.

Independent verification of PR #419 before integration: the four frozen hashes match; an independent decoder reproduces the DECODE line; lexical cover 0.404 with the verifier's own lexicon (25,681 forms from the repository's da-gutenberg corpus) against 0.157 for the best of 200 permuted keys (margin 0.247, the protocol declared +0.25; the contributor's run has 0.294) and 0.117 for the best of 200 sign shuffles; training cover 0.555. A crude blind annealer on the training transcription reached 19 of 29 sign values (best of 6 restarts). The writer's table on image 091 left confirmed at full size: 26 signs in three rows. Only 49 of 182 held-out reading words equal a mechanically decoded word (85% of characters agree): the frozen transcription has roughly 10% sign errors, and the 94.41% is a reader's classification.

Integration re-reading of the held-out images 030-031 at full size against the writer's table: eight of the 169 words the contributor classed read were misread (beholdt twice, read 'holdt'; 'for bestandig', read 'for Bøssen dig'; seer, read 'saae'; skeer, read 'skal'; Dem, read 'Den'; 'paa' supplied for a single sign p), so 161 of 179 words stood as delivered (89.9%). Also Maria written in full, 'ra' not on the page, Artilasia one word, Jom-fru and Kir-kegaard plain across line breaks, skjøn for '[?ssyon]'. After correction 172 of 176 words read, 1 supplied, 3 doubtful (Kabbe, karlegravet, søn); one reader with the key, not blind.

The nine first-session pages (003 R - 008 L; contributor 385 of 425 words at low resolution, 90.6%) re-read on the full-size images: complete text in reading.md Part 1; 437 of 447 words read (counted with cipher headings and each 'gange'), 1 supplied, 9 doubtful. Changed words include bløde (was flyde), denne Mand, svige (was [?værke]), træskelig bedrog, de[r]for vover. One reader with the key, not blind. The 136 pages of the second session were not re-read: no sign-level transcription exists for them.

outcome.method_basis: The key was found from guessed probable words (the trinitarian closing formula, 'gange' after the clear numeral 3, the cipher ordinals of the headings) and a blind annealing; no plaintext was at hand and the clear headings give only the subject. It was measured once on held-out images transcribed and hashed beforehand, and the writer's own alphabet table on image 091 left (a key in the volume, found afterwards by the contributor's record) gives the same values. An independent re-solution: Ferdinand Ohrt's unpublished decipherment is prior work, not consulted.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Held-out images 030-031 checked word by word on the full-size image at the integration (12 Nov 2026): 161 of the contributor's 179 words stood as delivered = 89.9% (he classed 169 as read, 94.41%; eight of those were misread). After correction 172 of 176 words on these pages are read, and 437 of 447 on the nine first pages re-read at full size (one reader with the key, not blind). The other 136 pages (7,451 words) carry only the contributor's classification, 95.4% (whole book 95.1%), which cannot be re-derived: no sign-level transcription exists.

texts.label: Kloge Søren's Cyprianus (DFS 1997/020), the charms in cipher, c. 1858
texts.summary: The working book of a Danish cunning man of Funen: about a hundred charms and recipes against bleeding, wounds, colic, toothache, fever and other ills; protection of cattle, horses, poultry, butter and milk against witchcraft; pests summoned to the Thing; guns bound and men made proof against shot; fire conjured; winning at cards; and a long series against thieves. The translation file is a summary table with a few charms in full. An earlier decipherment by Ferdinand Ohrt is recorded in the archive (not consulted).

reading_review.by: integration check (project), on the contributor's reading
reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the full-size images for twelve pages only: the held-out images 030-031 (eight misread words corrected; 172 of 176 words now read) and the nine first pages 003 R - 008 L (437 of 447). There the charms construe as Danish of the 1850s: a sacred precedent, 'saasandt som ... saasandt skal ...', the trinitarian close, then directions for use. The other 136 pages were read through as text but not against the images: they construe in the same frames, with holes concentrated on 064 L and 010 R, and no sign-level transcription exists to check them. Grade B: coherent but raw (unpunctuated, 1850s spelling), and unverified for most of the book. The contributor's own review (11 Nov 2026) also gave B.

outcome.notes: Independent re-solution: an earlier decipherment by Ferdinand Ohrt (1873-1938) is recorded in the archive by the contributor's quotation of the 1977 inventory; it has not been consulted and was not used. The key is also in the volume (the writer's table on 091 left); by the contributor's record it was found after the measurement. The contributor's folder holds no image; the site page carries two crops from the KB images, which the KB marks out of copyright. A private 20th-century piece, not part of the grimoire, is excluded.
